content.title: About
content.content: Mullet (family Mugilidae) is a freshwater and marine fish found in coastal zones of warm seas and rivers. It has an elongated body covered with large scales and a characteristic silvery coloration. The flesh is soft, tender, with a mild sea flavor, and is rich in protein and beneficial omega‑3 fatty acids.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mullet can change sex during its life: young individuals are usually males, later becoming females.
The fish can thrive in low‑salinity environments, making it common in river estuaries.
Mullet is a staple in traditional cuisines of the Mediterranean, Asia, and Africa.
In some regions the fish is nicknamed “multi‑mullet” because of its rapid reproduction rate.
Mullet is often farmed in aquaculture due to its high productivity and disease resistance.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Mullet provides about 18‑20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: It contains EPA and DHA, which promote heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mullet supplies vitamin B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The fish is a good source of selenium, phosphorus and potassium, aiding thyroid function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, mullet typically contains less mercury, making it a safer frequent choice.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including mullet.

items.title: Water contamination
items.content: Fish caught in polluted waters may contain heavy metals or microplastics; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Like any raw fish, mullet can harbor parasites; cooking to an internal temperature of 63 °C eliminates the risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mullet can be fried, baked, steamed, or used in stews and soups. Fillets are often marinated with lemon, garlic and herbs. For a lighter option, poach the fish and add it to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh mullet should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for no more than 2 days, preferably wrapped in food‑grade film. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Rinse the fish under cold running water before cooking.

fruit-flavored-drink-powdered-not-recons.title: Fruit Flavored Drink, Powdered, Not Reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: The fruit flavored drink in powder form (not reconstituted) is a dry blend of flavorings, sweeteners, and sometimes vitamin additives. The powder retains a bright fruit taste and aroma and can be used in culinary applications without adding water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Powdered drinks are convenient for transport and storage because they do not require a liquid component.
A wide range of flavors is available: orange, lemon, strawberry, mango, and more.
Some versions are fortified with vitamin C and other micronutrients.
The powder is often used in sports nutrition for a quick energy boost.
Unlike ready‑to‑drink beverages, the powder allows you to control concentration and calorie content.

items.title: Source of Vitamin C
items.content: Certain variants are enriched with vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Energy Support
items.content: Sugars and fast‑acting carbohydrates provide rapid replenishment of energy stores after exercise.

items.title: Convenient Consumption
items.content: The powder is easy to dose and add to foods, simplifying control over intake.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Most powders contain added sugars, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes or those limiting calories.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Flavorings or sweeteners in the blend can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Vitamin Overdose
items.content: Frequent consumption of fortified versions may lead to excess intake of certain vitamins, such as vitamin C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The powder can be mixed into yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, or baked goods. If desired, it can be dissolved in a small amount of water or juice, but this is not required.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping and loss of flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal is made from whole or processed oat grains, often served as a hot porridge. It is a popular fast‑food style breakfast that can be prepared in minutes by adding hot water or milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Oat flakes are produced by steaming and rolling whole oat kernels.
Oatmeal is frequently used in vegan and gluten‑free recipes when certified gluten‑free oats are chosen.
In the United States, oatmeal is among the most consumed breakfast foods, especially in instant forms.
Oats contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan may reduce LDL cholesterol and support immune function.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Oatmeal provides thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for bones, muscles, and nerves.

items.title: Low glycemic index when prepared properly
items.content: Oatmeal raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Although oats are naturally gluten‑free, they are often contaminated with wheat during processing; those with celiac disease need certified gluten‑free oats.

items.title: High glycemic index in instant varieties
items.content: Quick‑cooking flakes can raise blood sugar faster than whole‑grain oats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare oatmeal by pouring hot water or milk over the flakes and letting it sit for 2–5 minutes. Add fruit, nuts, honey, spices (cinnamon, vanilla) or use it as a base for smoothies and protein bars.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oat flakes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.

content.title: About
content.content: Diet cola is a calorie‑free carbonated soft drink flavored like regular cola but sweetened with artificial sweeteners instead of sugar. It retains the classic cola taste while providing virtually no calories, making it popular among weight‑conscious consumers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first diet cola, Diet Coke, was launched by Coca‑Cola in 1982.
Common sweeteners include acesulfame‑K, sucralose, and aspartame.
Diet colas are often used in cooking and baking to add cola flavor without added sugar.
Some countries regulate the use of certain artificial sweeteners in beverages.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A 330 ml serving typically contains 0–5 kcal, helping to maintain a balanced energy intake.

items.title: Sugar‑free
items.content: Does not raise blood glucose levels, making it suitable for people with diabetes when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any non‑alcoholic beverage, it contributes to daily fluid needs.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to aspartame, sucralose, or acesulfame‑K.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic pH can contribute to tooth enamel erosion with frequent consumption.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Most diet colas contain caffeine, which may affect sleep and cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink diet cola straight, use it in mixed drinks, mocktails, or recipes that call for cola flavor without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

vegetable-and-fruit-juice-drink-with-hig.title: Vegetable and Fruit Juice Drink with High Vitamin C

content.title: About
content.content: The vegetable and fruit juice drink with high vitamin C is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage made from a blend of fresh vegetables and fruits, enriched with vitamin C. It has a light taste, bright aroma, and contains minimal added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: One serving can provide up to 150 % of the daily recommended vitamin C intake.
The drink contains natural antioxidants derived from berries and leafy vegetables.
A light texture is achieved through advanced cold‑press technology.
No artificial colors or flavors are added.
It is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the body's defense mechanisms, helping to fight infections.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients from fruits and vegetables neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Improved hydration
items.content: Low calorie content and high water level aid in maintaining fluid balance.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C participates in collagen synthesis, promoting skin elasticity and a healthy complexion.

items.title: Reduced fatigue
items.content: A blend of B‑vitamins and minerals helps lessen feelings of tiredness.

items.title: Allergy to specific ingredients
items.content: The drink may contain fruits or vegetables that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High acidity
items.content: Large amounts of vitamin C can increase acidity, which may be unsuitable for gastritis patients.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although added sugar is minimal, natural fruit sugars are present.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume the drink chilled, straight from the bottle. It can be added to smoothies, used as a base for cocktails, or paired with light snacks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. After opening, consume within 3–5 days. Do not freeze.
